text: ‍BLOOMBERG: Mexico Murder Rate Plunges as Sheinbaum Targets Cartel Operators September 2, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Bloomberg credits Sheinbaum's strategy: intentional homicides down 51% since she took office, 44 fewer killings a day, July the lowest daily average in 11 years. 🇲🇽 Worth noting: the same outlet ran "Mexico Cartel Takedown Is a Risk for Sheinbaum" in February. 💵🇲🇽 <u>Remittances hit $5.57 billion in July — a sixth straight month of growth despite the US crackdown</u>

Mexicans abroad sent home $5,570.6 million in July, up about 3% year-on-year and the sixth consecutive monthly increase, according to Banxico figures reported by El Financiero. That lifts January–July to $36.3 billion, above the $35.2 billion of the same stretch in 2025 — even as ICE raids and visa purges target the very workers wiring the money. The average transfer held at $426, the paycheck millions of Mexican households still count on.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>The agency raiding Mexican communities just hired 12,000 agents with no background checks</u>

ICE — the force sweeping through Mexican and Latino neighborhoods across the US — brought on 12,000 new agents through an accelerated pipeline that skipped background checks entirely, per Regeneración. Unvetted, armed, and pushed toward arrest quotas, they're the same muscle behind the "cabotage" accusations and mass B1 visa cancellations now choking Mexican truckers at the border. Washington calls it enforcement; it's a hiring spree with no filter for who gets a badge and a gun.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Ex-Guerrero governor detained as Sheinbaum readies a new Ayotzinapa report</u>

Ahead of the case's 12th anniversary on September 26, Sheinbaum's government is preparing a fresh Ayotzinapa report built on new evidence and forensic methods — and it has already put former Guerrero governor Ángel Aguirre Rivero in custody, accused of concealing recordings tied to the students' disappearance. "Nadie está por encima de la ley," said Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez. Aguirre governed the state when the 43 were taken in 2014; the "verdad histórica" that shielded him is coming apart piece by piece.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>SAT cancels invoicing for 2,205 companies caught in the fuel-theft racket</u>

Mexico's tax authority yanked invoicing privileges from 2,205 companies that sold illegal fuel between October 2024 and August 2026 — shell "factureras" that, as Sheinbaum put it, "facturaban combustible cuando, en realidad, no transportaban combustible" (billed for fuel they never actually moved). Add 63 revoked customs-agent permits and a new fuel-traceability database shared across agencies, and customs revenue climbed roughly 250 billion pesos in 2025.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexican truckers shut the Mexicali–Calexico crossing over mass visa cancellations</u>

Mexican cargo drivers blockaded the commercial gate at Mexicali–Calexico this week after Washington pulled roughly 4,000 B1 visas from operators in the region — 17 in a single day, according to Canacar regional delegate Alfonso Millán. Drivers say ICE is hitting them with arbitrary "cabotage" accusations and a new English-proficiency demand, stripping the papers they need to move freight. They warn they'll keep the crossing closed "as long as necessary" and extend it to Tijuana and San Luis Río Colorado if the US won't explain the revocations.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Volkswagen guts 786 jobs at its Puebla plant</u>

Volkswagen just cut 786 workers at its Cuautlancingo plant in Puebla and suspended a full production shift — the first bite of a global plan to shed 50,000 jobs worldwide, approved by its board this week. The 13,000 VW workers in Mexico are learning what "foreign investment" means when Wolfsburg hits a crisis: the newest hires and clause-85 temps go first — 611 fired, 175 pushed into "voluntary" exits. Governor Alejandro Armenta says the state is weighing emergency aid for those let go.
